discovery.definition: Locate a specific record or item that matches stated criteria.

retrieval.definition: Obtain a specific value from a known or located record.

enumeration.definition: Obtain a count, list or ordering over a set of records.

curation.definition: Change attributes of an existing record, or add to or remove from the user's own working set (cart, wishlist).

availability.definition: Set up a notification, watch or subscription so the user is told when something changes.

service.definition: Submit a new request, ticket, issue, comment or pull request for others to act on.

identity.definition: Create an account or change the attributes or access of an account (contact data, credentials, login permission).

transaction.definition: Complete a consequential commitment that is costly or impossible to undo: place an order, merge a change, publish a release, delete a resource.

decision_rules: Label the TERMINAL goal. A find step that only reaches the target is instrumental, not a goal.
A first step is a separate goal only when its result is reported or used in the next step; then the task is a composite and carries an ordered goal_sequence.
Labels come from the task definition (ask and verification), never from traces.
Pre-authentication state is not a labeling factor.

tier_rule.critical: Terminal step changes an account's authentication-affecting attributes or access (email, phone, credentials, login permission, creating an account that gets access: ASVS 7.5.1), or is a highly sensitive transaction (ASVS 7.5.3).
tier_rule.elevated: Harm grows with volume (requests or content submitted for others to act on), or the task reads personal data.
tier_rule.standard: Reversible change to an existing record, preference or the user's own working set; reads that return no personal data. A change to a non-authentication attribute (for example a full name) is standard.
tier_rule.note: Tier is assigned per task. It is not a function of goal and site alone: retrieval splits by whether personal data is returned, and identity splits by which attribute changes.

open: segment_tiers for composites are not annotated

read.definition: Locate, inspect, or aggregate existing application records without mutating state.

modify.definition: Mutate attributes, workflow state, or user-scoped flags (cart, wishlist, watch/subscribe, thread comment) on an existing record.

create.definition: Instantiate a new business or operational record (issue, pull request, support ticket, incident, problem, or change request).

identity.definition: Create, update, or disable a user account, its contact/credential attributes, or its login permission.

transaction.definition: Execute a consequential, costly-to-reverse commitment: place an order, merge a pull request, publish a release, or delete a repository.
